Restate only the main (public) question.
Compute \(57 \times 39 - 25 \times 36\).

First, calculate \(57 \times 39\):
\[57 \times 39 = 57 \times (40 - 1) = 57 \times 40 - 57 \times 1 = 2280 - 57 = 2223.\]

Next, calculate \(25 \times 36\):
\[25 \times 36 = 25 \times (30 + 6) = 25 \times 30 + 25 \times 6 = 750 + 150 = 900.\]

Now, subtract the second product from the first:
\[2223 - 900 = 1323.\]

To double-check, let's verify the main result using an alternative order of operations:
Calculate \(25 \times 36\) again to confirm it is indeed 900.
Then, calculate \(57 \times 39\) again to confirm it is indeed 2223.
Finally, perform the subtraction once more:
\[2223 - 900 = 1323.\]

Both methods yield the same result, confirming the answer.
